headline: High-risk default interaction: nullclaw can read/write and use MCP/network, while LlamaFactory is non-runnable and isolated, making prompt-injection and leakage mainly one-way but still operationally dangerous.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can ingest files, web content, MCP, and stdin/stdout by default, so it can be steered by attacker-controlled content. LlamaFactory is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it is not a direct injector. The pairwise pathway exists through shared content passed into nullclaw, but the lack of a documented bridge from LlamaFactory lowers it below high.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory outputs are copied into nullclaw inputs or workspace files
IF nullclaw processes untrusted web, webhook, or MCP content as instructions
mitigations: Disable MCP and webhook ingestion in nullclaw for this pairing
Keep LlamaFactory outputs in a separate, read-only directory
Add a manual review step before nullclaw acts on any imported text
Use a prompt delimiter/template that strips instructions from imported content

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches secrets, workspace files, and audit logs, and it has broad network egress, so sensitive material can leave the local boundary. LlamaFactory itself has no filesystem or network surfaces, so it is not the leak source, but its outputs could be imported into nullclaw and then exposed. This is a default-config risk for nullclaw, with the pairwise interaction inferred rather than directly documented.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory-generated content includes secrets or customer data
IF nullclaw is configured to sync, upload, or forward workspace files or logs
mitigations: Exclude secrets from any shared workspace between the agents
Turn off or restrict nullclaw network egress for the shared task
Store imported artifacts in a redacted staging folder
Review audit-log retention and disable verbose logging for the session

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has unrestricted filesystem write, git modification, subprocess, and broad network capabilities, while LlamaFactory has no write or network capabilities. There is no direct write-write conflict, but if both are pointed at the same workspace or repo, nullclaw can overwrite artifacts produced for LlamaFactory. Uncertainty about the shared workspace escalates this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same writable workspace or git checkout
IF nullclaw is allowed to commit, rewrite, or regenerate files used by LlamaFactory
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent
Mount the LlamaFactory workspace read-only to nullclaw
Disable git write actions in nullclaw for the shared repo
Use file locks or a single-writer policy during handoff

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can act on files, webhooks, and scheduling, so if it consumes LlamaFactory output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. LlamaFactory is a model/fine-tuning tool with no built-in verification or downstream action controls shown here, so the pairwise chain is plausible but not directly evidenced. Because nullclaw has action-taking authority, the blast radius is more than a simple formatting error.
conditions: IF nullclaw uses LlamaFactory output as a source of facts or instructions
IF nullclaw triggers webhooks, emails, commits, or scheduled tasks from that output
mitigations: Require a verification step before nullclaw acts on LlamaFactory output
Mark LlamaFactory output as untrusted in the handoff format
Disable automatic execution of tasks derived from imported text
Log and review any downstream action triggered by model-generated content

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, conversation history, and workspace files, which creates compliance exposure if those data classes are processed under stricter regimes. LlamaFactory is docs-only and touches no data classes here, so the compliance concern is driven by nullclaw alone; the pairwise issue is that LlamaFactory outputs may be routed into a more sensitive compliance domain.
conditions: IF regulated data such as secrets, customer records, or conversation history is routed through nullclaw
IF retention or residency rules differ between the two agents' storage locations
mitigations: Classify and block regulated data from the shared workspace
Set short retention on nullclaw logs and memory for the session
Document which agent may store which data class
Use a separate environment for any regulated workload
